note: Adjudicated variants: two of orthography (the house i/j rule), three of punctuation and three of capitalization — eight in all. Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero further divergence.

adjudicated.ruling: The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
No comma before the apposition Dómini nostri, with handmissal-eo and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.suscipe-sancta-trinitas w016: ejúsdem Christi Fílii tui Dómini nostri is one unbroken title.
No comma between the title and the genitives it possesses, with handmissal-eo: tam beátæ passiónis depends on the same chain and is not parenthetical.

The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
No comma before the ac joining the second ablative, with do and with the corpus rulings at ordinarium.confiteor w028 and ordinarium.lavabo w024: donis ac datis is one pair.

Lowercase, with handmissal-eo and with the typical edition. The capital in do marks the three blessings that fall on the word, which this edition carries as rubric segments instead. The same ruling governs w045 and w047.
